126	# ─── [SPEC-3][change] the SIGINT path ─────────────────────────────────────
127	# #1850 (ADR-054 §4, ADR-025): the SIGINT path is the recorded abort word, not
128	# rc=130 — a bare 130 from a stage is just a failed stage now. So the stage
129	# does what a Ctrl-C does to the process group: the sentinel is armed (empty =
130	# sigint) and the child dies with 130. The run must end on the abort path —
131	# exit 1, status interrupted — or this case would only repeat SPEC-2.
132	print_test_section "[SPEC-3][change] release runs on the SIGINT path (abort word sigint)"
133	_arm_release
134	# shellcheck disable=SC2016  # expanded by the stage at run time, not here
135	_arm_outcome ': > "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR/.abort.signal"' 130
136	_run_case "rc130" skip
137	assert_file_exists "[SPEC-3] release ran on the SIGINT path" "$RELEASE_MARKER"
138	assert_eq "[SPEC-3] the run took the abort path: exit 1 (not 130), status interrupted" \
139	    "1 interrupted" "$_CASE_RC $(jq -r '.status // "MISSING"' "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/state-rc130/pipeline-state.json" 2>/dev/null)"
140	
141	# ─── [SPEC-4][change] SIGTERM delivered to the runner itself ───────────────
142	# Distinct from SPEC-3: there the stage returned a code, here the signal is
143	# delivered to the runner process while a stage is still executing. #1759's
144	# re-armed INT/TERM traps are what give this path somewhere to hang off.
145	print_test_section "[SPEC-4][change] release runs when the runner is SIGTERMed mid-stage"
146	_arm_release; _arm_outcome "sleep 30" 0
147	rm -f "$RELEASE_MARKER" "$RELEASE_ENTERED"
148	export ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/state-sigterm"
149	export STAGE_STARTED="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/stage-started-sigterm"
150	rm -f "$STAGE_STARTED"
151	mkdir -p "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR"
152	( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && bash "$RUNNER" --template always-run-minimal \
153	    --goal "always-run sigterm" ) >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/sigterm.out" 2>&1 &
154	_runner_pid=$!
155	# Wait for the run to actually reach the stage before signalling — signalling a
156	# runner still in startup would prove nothing about the exit path.
157	#
158	# #2029: this used to wait for `pipeline-state.json` and then sleep 1. That file
159	# is written during STARTUP, so the wait proved nothing and the sleep was the only
160	# real margin. Under load it was not enough and the signal landed mid-startup.
161	# STAGE_STARTED is written by the stage itself, so it cannot be reached early.
162	_waited=0
163	while [[ ! -f "$STAGE_STARTED" && $_waited -lt 300 ]]; do
164	    sleep 0.2; _waited=$(( _waited + 1 ))
165	done
166	if [[ ! -f "$STAGE_STARTED" ]]; then
167	    assert_fail "[SPEC-4] the stage started before the signal was sent" \
168	        "STAGE_STARTED never appeared in 60s — the run never reached a stage, so the exit path was never exercised"
169	fi
170	_spec4_t0=$(date +%s)
171	kill -TERM "$_runner_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
172	wait "$_runner_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
173	_spec4_wait_s=$(( $(date +%s) - _spec4_t0 ))
174	# The trap runs in the dying process; give it a moment to land the marker.
175	_waited=0
176	while [[ ! -f "$RELEASE_MARKER" && $_waited -lt 50 ]]; do
177	    sleep 0.2; _waited=$(( _waited + 1 ))
178	done
179	
180	# #2029: say WHAT WAS SEEN, not merely that the file is absent.
181	#
182	# This assertion has failed intermittently on CI for as long as it has existed,
183	# and it could never be diagnosed because "file not found" is the same output
184	# whether the runner ignored the signal, died before its trap, ran teardown into
185	# a different path, or simply had not finished yet. Three separate mechanisms
186	# were proposed for it and all three were disproven.
187	#
188	# The sibling assertion in runner-release-exit-paths prints the marker it read,
189	# and that one line is what let #2046 identify its cause in minutes after days of
190	# guessing. This is that lesson applied here: the next occurrence explains itself
191	# instead of starting another hunt.
192	if [[ ! -f "$RELEASE_MARKER" ]]; then
193	    {
194	        printf '  DIAGNOSTIC [SPEC-4]: release marker absent after %ss of polling\n' "$(( _waited * 2 / 10 ))"
195	        printf '    wait on the runner returned after: %ss\n' "$_spec4_wait_s"
196	        printf '    runner pid %s still alive: %s\n' "$_runner_pid" \
197	            "$(kill -0 "$_runner_pid" 2>/dev/null && echo YES || echo no)"
198	        printf '    release hook ENTERED marker: %s\n' \
199	            "$([[ -f "$RELEASE_ENTERED" ]] && echo present || echo absent)"
200	        printf '    state dir: %s\n' \
201	            "$([[ -d "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR" ]] && (cd "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR" && printf '%s ' * 2>/dev/null) || echo '<missing>')"
202	        printf '    runner output (last 5 lines):\n'
203	        tail -5 "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/sigterm.out" 2>/dev/null | sed 's/^/      /' || printf '      <no output>\n'
204	    } >&2
205	fi
206	# RELEASE_ENTERED separates "the hook never started" from "it started and did not
207	# finish" — the single most useful split, and the one the bare check cannot make.
208	assert_file_exists "[SPEC-4] release ran after SIGTERM to the runner" "$RELEASE_MARKER"
209	
210	# ─── [SPEC-5][guard] a hanging release cannot hang the exit ────────────────
211	# The stage declares timeout_s: 2. A hook that blocks past it must be killed and
212	# the exit must continue — otherwise Ctrl-C becomes a lockup, which is the exact
213	# class of bug an EXIT-trap dispatch exists to avoid. Asserting the WALL CLOCK
214	# rather than the marker: the marker would also be absent if release never ran
215	# at all, so it cannot distinguish "bounded" from "broken".
216	print_test_section "[SPEC-5][guard] a release hook that hangs is bounded by its timeout_s"
217	_arm_release "sleep 60"; _arm_outcome "" 0
218	rm -f "$RELEASE_MARKER" "$RELEASE_ENTERED"
219	export ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/state-hang"
220	mkdir -p "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR"
221	_t0=$(date +%s)
222	set +e
223	( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && bash "$RUNNER" --template always-run-minimal \
224	    --goal "always-run hang" ) >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/hang.out" 2>&1
225	set -e
226	_elapsed=$(( $(date +%s) - _t0 ))
227	# 45s is generous against a 2s bound plus runner startup; the assertion is
228	# "bounded at all", not a tight budget — a tight one would flake under a loaded
229	# parallel pool (the #991 lesson).
230	if [[ "$_elapsed" -lt 45 ]]; then
231	    assert_pass "[SPEC-5] a 60s release hook did not hold the exit (${_elapsed}s)"
232	else
233	    assert_fail "[SPEC-5] a 60s release hook held the exit" "elapsed=${_elapsed}s"
234	fi
235	# These two together are what make the case meaningful: the hook WAS entered
236	# (so the bound is what stopped it) and did NOT complete (so it was actually
237	# killed). Either alone is satisfied by a dispatch that never happened.
238	assert_file_exists "[SPEC-5] the hanging hook was actually dispatched" "$RELEASE_ENTERED"
239	assert_file_not_exists "[SPEC-5] the hanging hook was killed before completing" "$RELEASE_MARKER"
240	
241	# ─── [#1801/SPEC-5]: persist always_run stage bounded by timeout_s: (not 120s) ─
242	# _runner_dispatch_always_run must use template_stage_time_limit (top-level
243	# timeout_s:) instead of ZBUILD_RELEASE_TIMEOUT / router.timeout_s.
244	# The fixture template sets persist.timeout_s: 4 (new code reads) and
245	# persist.router.timeout_s: 120 (old code reads ZBUILD_RELEASE_TIMEOUT / router.timeout_s).
246	# A blocking persist hook must be killed in ~4s, NOT ~120s.
247	# FAILS on old code (elapsed ~120s > 20), PASSES on new code (elapsed ~4s < 20).
248	print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-5] persist always_run watchdog uses timeout_s: not router.timeout_s: 120"
249	mkdir -p "$PLUGINS_ROOT/tool/persist"
250	cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/tool/persist/manifest.yaml" <<'MF'
251	id: persist
252	name: Persist Stub Spec5
253	kind: tool
254	version: 0.0.1
255	hooks:
256	  run: persist_run
257	requires:
258	  core:
259	    - redaction
260	provides:
261	  role: persist
262	MF
263	_SPEC5P_ENTERED="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/spec5p-entered"
264	_SPEC5P_DONE="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/spec5p-done"
265	cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/tool/persist/plugin.sh" <<PLUG
266	persist_run() {
267	    : > "${_SPEC5P_ENTERED}"
268	    sleep 120
269	    : > "${_SPEC5P_DONE}"
270	    return 0
271	}
272	PLUG
273	
274	_spec5p_repo="$(setup_git_temp_repo "always-run-spec5p")"
275	install_template_overlay "$_spec5p_repo" always-run-minimal
276	if [[ -d "$_spec5p_repo/.git/info" ]] && \
277	   ! grep -qxF '/.zbuild/' "$_spec5p_repo/.git/info/exclude" 2>/dev/null; then
278	    printf '/.zbuild/\n' >> "$_spec5p_repo/.git/info/exclude"
279	fi
280	cat > "$_spec5p_repo/.zbuild/templates/always-run-spec5p.yaml" <<'YAML'
281	id: always-run-spec5p
282	extends: always-run-minimal
283	always_run:
284	  - release
285	  - persist
286	persist:
287	  gate: auto
288	  roles: [persist]
289	  timeout_s: 4
290	  router:
291	    timeout_s: 120
292	  io:
293	    destinations: [file]
294	    tail_lines: 50
295	YAML
296	_arm_outcome "" 0
297	_arm_release
298	rm -f "$_SPEC5P_ENTERED" "$_SPEC5P_DONE"
299	export ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/state-spec5p"
300	export ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/events/spec5p-events.jsonl"
301	mkdir -p "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR"
302	_spec5p_t0=$(date +%s)
303	set +e
304	( cd "$_spec5p_repo" && bash "$RUNNER" --template always-run-spec5p \
305	    --goal "spec5-persist" ) >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/spec5p.out" 2>&1
306	set -e
307	_spec5p_elapsed=$(( $(date +%s) - _spec5p_t0 ))
308	if [[ "$_spec5p_elapsed" -lt 20 ]]; then
309	    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-5] persist always_run watchdog bounds at timeout_s: 4 (exited in ${_spec5p_elapsed}s; old code: router.timeout_s: 120)"
310	else
311	    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-5] persist always_run watchdog must use timeout_s: 4" \
312	        "runner took ${_spec5p_elapsed}s; expected < 20s (timeout_s: 4); old code reads router.timeout_s: 120 → ~120s"
313	fi
314	assert_file_exists "[#1801/SPEC-5] persist hook was entered (always_run persist stage dispatched)" "$_SPEC5P_ENTERED"
315	assert_file_not_exists "[#1801/SPEC-5] persist hook killed before completing (bounded by timeout_s: 4, not 120s)" "$_SPEC5P_DONE"
316	
317	# ─── [SPEC-6][guard] an unresolvable always-run role is LOUD ───────────────
318	# The code this replaces did `[[ -d "$_td_dir" ]] || return 0` — a missing
319	# plugin was a silent no-op. An always-run stage that cannot be resolved has not
320	# run, and the operator must be able to see that rather than infer it from a
321	# missing effect.
322	print_test_section "[SPEC-6][guard] an unresolvable role emits an event instead of failing silently"
323	_arm_outcome "" 0
324	rm -f "$RELEASE_MARKER"
325	rm -rf "$PLUGINS_ROOT/tool/teardown"
326	export ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/state-unresolved"
327	export ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/events/unresolved.jsonl"
328	mkdir -p "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR"
329	set +e
330	( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && bash "$RUNNER" --template always-run-minimal \
331	    --goal "always-run unresolved" ) >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/unresolved.out" 2>&1
332	_unres_rc=$?
333	set -e
334	assert_event_emitted "[SPEC-6] stage.always_run.unresolved is emitted" \
335	    "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL" "stage.always_run.unresolved"
336	# And it must not change the run's fate — an always-run stage never decides the
337	# verdict, including when it could not be found.
338	assert_eq "[SPEC-6] an unresolvable always-run stage does not fail the run" "0" "$_unres_rc"
339	
340	# [#1801/SPEC-5] static: always-run-minimal.yaml carries timeout_s: at stage level
341	# template_stage_time_limits_load matches `timeout_s:` at stage-level indent
342	# (exactly 2 spaces from the stage name at column 0). It must NOT be under
343	# `router:` (4-space indent) — that is the old path this change removes.
344	#
345	# Old code: always-run-minimal.yaml might only have timeout_s inside router: → awk
346	#   finds nothing at 2-space indent → extracted value empty/wrong → FAILS ✓
347	# New code: timeout_s: 2 is present as a direct child of release: → PASSES ✓
348	print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-5] static: always-run-minimal.yaml release.timeout_s at stage level"
349	
350	_ARM_FIXTURE="$REPO_ROOT/tests/fixtures/templates/always-run-minimal.yaml"
351	
352	# Extract stage-level timeout_s: for release: (exactly 2-space indent, not inside router:)
353	_arm_release_ts="$(awk '
354	    /^release:/{in_r=1;in_sub=0;next}
355	    in_r && /^[a-zA-Z]/{in_r=0}
356	    in_r && /^  [a-zA-Z]/ && !/^  timeout_s:/{
357	        if ($0 ~ /^  router:/) { in_sub=1 } else { in_sub=0 }
358	        next
359	    }
360	    in_r && !in_sub && /^  timeout_s:/{
361	        sub(/^[[:space:]]*timeout_s:[[:space:]]*/, ""); print; exit
362	    }
363	' "$_ARM_FIXTURE" 2>/dev/null || printf '')"
364	
365	if [[ "$_arm_release_ts" == "2" ]]; then
366	    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-5] always-run-minimal.yaml: release.timeout_s is 2 at stage level (not under router:)"
367	else
368	    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-5] always-run-minimal.yaml: release.timeout_s must be 2 as direct stage child" \
369	        "got: '${_arm_release_ts:-<not found>}'; old code reads router.timeout_s; template_stage_time_limits_load needs 2-space indent"
370	fi
371	
372	print_test_results
373

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Integration: #1831 — an `always_run:` stage runs on EVERY exit path.
#
# This is the assertion the attribute exists for. A mechanism that fires on four
# of five exit paths is #1878's defect wearing a new name ("the snapshot was
# never called"), so each path gets its own case and names itself on failure —
# a single parameterised assertion would report "one of five" and leave the
# operator to find which.
#
# Paths covered: rc=0, rc=1, a stage killed by SIGINT (rc=130 + the recorded
# abort word), SIGTERM to the runner, and a release hook that hangs past its
# own timeout_s.
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
RUNNER="$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/runner.sh"

# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"

print_test_header "always_run dispatches on every exit path (#1831)"
setup_test_env "zb-always-run-exit"
export ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=warn

PLUGINS_ROOT="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/plugins"
export ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT="$PLUGINS_ROOT"
export ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/events"
export ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL="$ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR/events.jsonl"
export ZBUILD_EVENT_SCHEMA="$REPO_ROOT/config/event-schema.json"
export ZBUILD_MODELS_FILE="$REPO_ROOT/config/models.json"
export ZBUILD_CYCLES_ENABLED=0
export ZBUILD_SCOPE_OVERRIDE=1
mkdir -p "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR" "$HOME/.zbuild"
printf '%s' "bootstrap" > "$HOME/.zbuild/scope-override-token"

OVERLAY_REPO="$(setup_git_temp_repo always-run-overlay)"
install_template_overlay "$OVERLAY_REPO" always-run-minimal

# The always-run plugin, bound by ROLE (not by directory — that coupling is
# what #1831 removes). It touches a marker so "did it run?" is a file test
# rather than an inference from an event that might not be emitted.
mock_plugin_factory "outcome"  "agent" 0 "" ""         >/dev/null
mock_plugin_factory "teardown" "tool"  0 "" "teardown" >/dev/null

RELEASE_MARKER="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/release-ran"
RELEASE_ENTERED="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/release-entered"
_arm_release() {
    # Two markers, not one. ENTERED is written before the optional sleep,
    # RAN after it. With a single completion marker, "the watchdog killed a
    # hanging hook" and "the hook was never dispatched at all" are the same
    # observation — and SPEC-5 passed for that wrong reason during development,
    # before the dispatch worked at all.
    # $1 = optional `sleep N` injected between the two, for the watchdog case.
    cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/tool/teardown/plugin.sh" <<PLUG
teardown_run() {
    : > "${RELEASE_ENTERED}"
    ${1:-:}
    : > "${RELEASE_MARKER}"
    return 0
}
PLUG
}

# The stage announces that it is RUNNING (#2029). `pipeline-state.json` appears
# during startup, long before any stage is dispatched, so waiting on it and then
# sleeping a second is not "the stage has started" — it is a guess that happens to
# hold on an idle machine.
#
# On a loaded one it does not, and SPEC-4 then SIGTERMs a runner still setting up
# its worktree: no stage has run, no release hook is armed, no marker is written,
# and the assertion reports a missing file with no hint that the run never got
# that far. Observed directly — `wait` returned in 0s, the hook-entered marker was
# absent, and the runner's last line was "Working in the run's worktree".
#
# `runner-release-exit-paths-test.sh` already does this correctly with
# BUILD_STARTED; this is the same idea. The marker can only appear once the stage
# is genuinely executing, so load can only delay it, never fake it.
# #1850: the stage writes the v2 result its manifest (mock_plugin_factory's)
# promises — pass on rc 0, error/broken otherwise — so a run that should succeed
# is not failed for leaving no readable result.
_arm_outcome() {
    local _o=pass
    [[ "${2:-0}" -ne 0 ]] && _o=broken
    cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/agent/outcome/plugin.sh" <<PLUG
outcome_run() {
    : > "\${STAGE_STARTED:-/dev/null}"
    ${1:-:}
    $(mock_result_line outcome "$_o")
    return ${2:-0}
}
PLUG
}

# Each case gets its own state dir: a stale marker or state file from a prior
# case would make a later one pass for the wrong reason.
_run_case() {
    local name="$1" rc_want_set="$2"
    rm -f "$RELEASE_MARKER" "$RELEASE_ENTERED"
    export ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/state-$name"
    mkdir -p "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR"
    set +e
    ( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && bash "$RUNNER" --template always-run-minimal \
        --goal "always-run $name" ) >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/$name.out" 2>&1
    _CASE_RC=$?
    set -e
    [[ "$rc_want_set" == "skip" ]] || true
}

# ─── [SPEC-1][change] rc=0 — the ordinary success path ──────────────────────
print_test_section "[SPEC-1][change] release runs when the pipeline succeeds"
_arm_release; _arm_outcome "" 0
_run_case "rc0" skip
assert_file_exists "[SPEC-1] release ran on rc=0" "$RELEASE_MARKER"

# ─── [SPEC-2][change] rc=1 — a failed run still frees its resources ─────────
# The failing path is the one that matters most: a run that died is exactly the
# run holding process groups and locks nobody else will clean up.
print_test_section "[SPEC-2][change] release runs when a stage fails"
_arm_release; _arm_outcome "" 1
_run_case "rc1" skip
assert_file_exists "[SPEC-2] release ran on a non-zero stage rc" "$RELEASE_MARKER"

# ─── [SPEC-3][change] the SIGINT path ─────────────────────────────────────
# #1850 (ADR-054 §4, ADR-025): the SIGINT path is the recorded abort word, not
# rc=130 — a bare 130 from a stage is just a failed stage now. So the stage
# does what a Ctrl-C does to the process group: the sentinel is armed (empty =
# sigint) and the child dies with 130. The run must end on the abort path —
# exit 1, status interrupted — or this case would only repeat SPEC-2.
print_test_section "[SPEC-3][change] release runs on the SIGINT path (abort word sigint)"
_arm_release
# shellcheck disable=SC2016  # expanded by the stage at run time, not here
_arm_outcome ': > "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR/.abort.signal"' 130
_run_case "rc130" skip
assert_file_exists "[SPEC-3] release ran on the SIGINT path" "$RELEASE_MARKER"
assert_eq "[SPEC-3] the run took the abort path: exit 1 (not 130), status interrupted" \
    "1 interrupted" "$_CASE_RC $(jq -r '.status // "MISSING"' "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/state-rc130/pipeline-state.json" 2>/dev/null)"

# ─── [SPEC-4][change] SIGTERM delivered to the runner itself ───────────────
# Distinct from SPEC-3: there the stage returned a code, here the signal is
# delivered to the runner process while a stage is still executing. #1759's
# re-armed INT/TERM traps are what give this path somewhere to hang off.
print_test_section "[SPEC-4][change] release runs when the runner is SIGTERMed mid-stage"
_arm_release; _arm_outcome "sleep 30" 0
rm -f "$RELEASE_MARKER" "$RELEASE_ENTERED"
export ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/state-sigterm"
export STAGE_STARTED="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/stage-started-sigterm"
rm -f "$STAGE_STARTED"
mkdir -p "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR"
( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && bash "$RUNNER" --template always-run-minimal \
    --goal "always-run sigterm" ) >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/sigterm.out" 2>&1 &
_runner_pid=$!
# Wait for the run to actually reach the stage before signalling — signalling a
# runner still in startup would prove nothing about the exit path.
#
# #2029: this used to wait for `pipeline-state.json` and then sleep 1. That file
# is written during STARTUP, so the wait proved nothing and the sleep was the only
# real margin. Under load it was not enough and the signal landed mid-startup.
# STAGE_STARTED is written by the stage itself, so it cannot be reached early.
_waited=0
while [[ ! -f "$STAGE_STARTED" && $_waited -lt 300 ]]; do
    sleep 0.2; _waited=$(( _waited + 1 ))
done
if [[ ! -f "$STAGE_STARTED" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[SPEC-4] the stage started before the signal was sent" \
        "STAGE_STARTED never appeared in 60s — the run never reached a stage, so the exit path was never exercised"
fi
_spec4_t0=$(date +%s)
kill -TERM "$_runner_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
wait "$_runner_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
_spec4_wait_s=$(( $(date +%s) - _spec4_t0 ))
# The trap runs in the dying process; give it a moment to land the marker.
_waited=0
while [[ ! -f "$RELEASE_MARKER" && $_waited -lt 50 ]]; do
    sleep 0.2; _waited=$(( _waited + 1 ))
done

# #2029: say WHAT WAS SEEN, not merely that the file is absent.
#
# This assertion has failed intermittently on CI for as long as it has existed,
# and it could never be diagnosed because "file not found" is the same output
# whether the runner ignored the signal, died before its trap, ran teardown into
# a different path, or simply had not finished yet. Three separate mechanisms
# were proposed for it and all three were disproven.
#
# The sibling assertion in runner-release-exit-paths prints the marker it read,
# and that one line is what let #2046 identify its cause in minutes after days of
# guessing. This is that lesson applied here: the next occurrence explains itself
# instead of starting another hunt.
if [[ ! -f "$RELEASE_MARKER" ]]; then
    {
        printf '  DIAGNOSTIC [SPEC-4]: release marker absent after %ss of polling\n' "$(( _waited * 2 / 10 ))"
        printf '    wait on the runner returned after: %ss\n' "$_spec4_wait_s"
        printf '    runner pid %s still alive: %s\n' "$_runner_pid" \
            "$(kill -0 "$_runner_pid" 2>/dev/null && echo YES || echo no)"
        printf '    release hook ENTERED marker: %s\n' \
            "$([[ -f "$RELEASE_ENTERED" ]] && echo present || echo absent)"
        printf '    state dir: %s\n' \
            "$([[ -d "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR" ]] && (cd "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR" && printf '%s ' * 2>/dev/null) || echo '<missing>')"
        printf '    runner output (last 5 lines):\n'
        tail -5 "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/sigterm.out" 2>/dev/null | sed 's/^/      /' || printf '      <no output>\n'
    } >&2
fi
# RELEASE_ENTERED separates "the hook never started" from "it started and did not
# finish" — the single most useful split, and the one the bare check cannot make.
assert_file_exists "[SPEC-4] release ran after SIGTERM to the runner" "$RELEASE_MARKER"

# ─── [SPEC-5][guard] a hanging release cannot hang the exit ────────────────
# The stage declares timeout_s: 2. A hook that blocks past it must be killed and
# the exit must continue — otherwise Ctrl-C becomes a lockup, which is the exact
# class of bug an EXIT-trap dispatch exists to avoid. Asserting the WALL CLOCK
# rather than the marker: the marker would also be absent if release never ran
# at all, so it cannot distinguish "bounded" from "broken".
print_test_section "[SPEC-5][guard] a release hook that hangs is bounded by its timeout_s"
_arm_release "sleep 60"; _arm_outcome "" 0
rm -f "$RELEASE_MARKER" "$RELEASE_ENTERED"
export ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/state-hang"
mkdir -p "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR"
_t0=$(date +%s)
set +e
( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && bash "$RUNNER" --template always-run-minimal \
    --goal "always-run hang" ) >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/hang.out" 2>&1
set -e
_elapsed=$(( $(date +%s) - _t0 ))
# 45s is generous against a 2s bound plus runner startup; the assertion is
# "bounded at all", not a tight budget — a tight one would flake under a loaded
# parallel pool (the #991 lesson).
if [[ "$_elapsed" -lt 45 ]]; then
    assert_pass "[SPEC-5] a 60s release hook did not hold the exit (${_elapsed}s)"
else
    assert_fail "[SPEC-5] a 60s release hook held the exit" "elapsed=${_elapsed}s"
fi
# These two together are what make the case meaningful: the hook WAS entered
# (so the bound is what stopped it) and did NOT complete (so it was actually
# killed). Either alone is satisfied by a dispatch that never happened.
assert_file_exists "[SPEC-5] the hanging hook was actually dispatched" "$RELEASE_ENTERED"
assert_file_not_exists "[SPEC-5] the hanging hook was killed before completing" "$RELEASE_MARKER"

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-5]: persist always_run stage bounded by timeout_s: (not 120s) ─
# _runner_dispatch_always_run must use template_stage_time_limit (top-level
# timeout_s:) instead of ZBUILD_RELEASE_TIMEOUT / router.timeout_s.
# The fixture template sets persist.timeout_s: 4 (new code reads) and
# persist.router.timeout_s: 120 (old code reads ZBUILD_RELEASE_TIMEOUT / router.timeout_s).
# A blocking persist hook must be killed in ~4s, NOT ~120s.
# FAILS on old code (elapsed ~120s > 20), PASSES on new code (elapsed ~4s < 20).

mkdir -p "$PLUGINS_ROOT/tool/persist"
cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/tool/persist/manifest.yaml" <<'MF'
id: persist
name: Persist Stub Spec5
kind: tool
version: 0.0.1
hooks:
  run: persist_run
requires:
  core:
    - redaction

  role: persist

cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/tool/persist/plugin.sh" <<PLUG
persist_run() {
    : > "${_SPEC5P_ENTERED}"
    sleep 120
    : > "${_SPEC5P_DONE}"
    return 0

PLUG

_spec5p_repo="$(setup_git_temp_repo "always-run-spec5p")"
install_template_overlay "$_spec5p_repo" always-run-minimal
if [[ -d "$_spec5p_repo/.git/info" ]] && \
   ! grep -qxF '/.zbuild/' "$_spec5p_repo/.git/info/exclude" 2>/dev/null; then
    printf '/.zbuild/\n' >> "$_spec5p_repo/.git/info/exclude"
fi
cat > "$_spec5p_repo/.zbuild/templates/always-run-spec5p.yaml" <<'YAML'

extends: always-run-minimal
always_run:
  - release
  - persist

  gate: auto
  roles: [persist]

    timeout_s: 120

_arm_outcome "" 0
_arm_release
rm -f "$_SPEC5P_ENTERED" "$_SPEC5P_DONE"

export ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/events/spec5p-events.jsonl"

# The code this replaces did `[[ -d "$_td_dir" ]] || return 0` — a missing
# plugin was a silent no-op. An always-run stage that cannot be resolved has not
# run, and the operator must be able to see that rather than infer it from a
# missing effect.
print_test_section "[SPEC-6][guard] an unresolvable role emits an event instead of failing silently"

rm -rf "$PLUGINS_ROOT/tool/teardown"

export ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/events/unresolved.jsonl"
mkdir -p "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR"
set +e
( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && bash "$RUNNER" --template always-run-minimal \
    --goal "always-run unresolved" ) >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/unresolved.out" 2>&1
_unres_rc=$?
set -e
assert_event_emitted "[SPEC-6] stage.always_run.unresolved is emitted" \
    "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL" "stage.always_run.unresolved"
# And it must not change the run's fate — an always-run stage never decides the
# verdict, including when it could not be found.
assert_eq "[SPEC-6] an unresolvable always-run stage does not fail the run" "0" "$_unres_rc"

# [#1801/SPEC-5] static: always-run-minimal.yaml carries timeout_s: at stage level
# template_stage_time_limits_load matches `timeout_s:` at stage-level indent
# (exactly 2 spaces from the stage name at column 0). It must NOT be under
# `router:` (4-space indent) — that is the old path this change removes.
#
# Old code: always-run-minimal.yaml might only have timeout_s inside router: → awk
#   finds nothing at 2-space indent → extracted value empty/wrong → FAILS ✓
# New code: timeout_s: 2 is present as a direct child of release: → PASSES ✓
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-5] static: always-run-minimal.yaml release.timeout_s at stage level"

_ARM_FIXTURE="$REPO_ROOT/tests/fixtures/templates/always-run-minimal.yaml"

# Extract stage-level timeout_s: for release: (exactly 2-space indent, not inside router:)
_arm_release_ts="$(awk '
    /^release:/{in_r=1;in_sub=0;next}
    in_r && /^[a-zA-Z]/{in_r=0}
    in_r && /^  [a-zA-Z]/ && !/^  timeout_s:/{
        if ($0 ~ /^  router:/) { in_sub=1 } else { in_sub=0 }
        next
    }
    in_r && !in_sub && /^  timeout_s:/{
        sub(/^[[:space:]]*timeout_s:[[:space:]]*/, ""); print; exit
    }
' "$_ARM_FIXTURE" 2>/dev/null || printf '')"

if [[ "$_arm_release_ts" == "2" ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-5] always-run-minimal.yaml: release.timeout_s is 2 at stage level (not under router:)"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-5] always-run-minimal.yaml: release.timeout_s must be 2 as direct stage child" \
        "got: '${_arm_release_ts:-<not found>}'; old code reads router.timeout_s; template_stage_time_limits_load needs 2-space indent"
fi

print_test_results

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Integration test (#1829, ADR-054 §7): the runner dispatches cleanup(release)
3	# on EVERY exit path from a run — success, non-zero rc, the SIGINT propagation
4	# chain, an external SIGTERM, and an external timeout.
5	#
6	# This is the acceptance criterion the mechanism exists for: a stage's live
7	# resources must be freed however the run ends. A single missed exit path leaks
8	# whatever that stage spawned (#1748: suites observed alive 15+ min after exit).
9	#
10	# Why SIGINT is driven by the stage rather than `kill -INT`: this harness starts
11	# non-interactively with SIGINT inherited as SIG_IGN, and POSIX forbids a child
12	# from un-ignoring it — so `kill -INT` is silently dropped and the assertion
13	# would pass standalone while proving nothing. The repo's existing
14	# sigint-aborts-pipeline-test.sh drives the same chain the same way: the child
15	# returns 130, which is exactly what the kernel produces on Ctrl-C. Since #1850
16	# (ADR-054 §4, ADR-025) a signal is a recorded WORD, not an rc, so the stage
17	# also arms the abort sentinel (empty = sigint), as the runner's INT trap in
18	# the process group would.
19	#
20	# Assertion in every case: the stub stages' cleanup hooks recorded `release`
21	# (and never `purge`) in the marker file.

288	    "$(jq -r 'select(.type=="pipeline.aborted") | .data.reason // empty' "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL" 2>/dev/null | sort -u | tr -d '\n')"
289	_assert_released "SPEC-3" intake build
290	
291	# ── SPEC-4: external SIGTERM ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
292	print_test_section "SPEC-4: exit path = external SIGTERM"
293	_prep sigterm
294	export BUILD_RC=0 BUILD_SLEEP=1
295	if command -v setsid >/dev/null 2>&1; then
296	    setsid bash -c 'cd "$1" && exec bash "$2" --template resume-minimal --goal "$3"' \
297	        _ "$OVERLAY_REPO" "$RUNNER" "release-sigterm" >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1 &
298	    RUNNER_PID=$!
299	else
300	    set -m
301	    bash -c 'cd "$1" && exec bash "$2" --template resume-minimal --goal "$3"' \
302	        _ "$OVERLAY_REPO" "$RUNNER" "release-sigterm" >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1 &
303	    RUNNER_PID=$!
304	    set +m
305	fi
306	for _ in $(seq 1 300); do [[ -s "$BUILD_STARTED" ]] && break; sleep 0.1; done
307	_build_pid="$(head -n 1 "$BUILD_STARTED" 2>/dev/null || true)"
308	_t0=$(date +%s)
309	kill -TERM "$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
310	wait "$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
311	_elapsed=$(( $(date +%s) - _t0 ))
312	# ADR-054 §7: the runner acts on the signal while the stage is still running.
313	# Build holds for 30s; a runner that waits for it to return took 30s+ here.
314	if [[ "$_elapsed" -lt 15 ]]; then
315	    assert_pass "[SPEC-4] the runner stops without waiting for the stage (${_elapsed}s)"
316	else
317	    assert_fail "[SPEC-4] the runner stops without waiting for the stage" "took ${_elapsed}s; build holds 30s"
318	fi
319	if [[ -n "$_build_pid" ]] && kill -0 "$_build_pid" 2>/dev/null; then
320	    assert_fail "[SPEC-4] the stage does not outlive the run" "build pid $_build_pid still alive"
321	    kill -KILL "$_build_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
322	else
323	    assert_pass "[SPEC-4] the stage does not outlive the run"
324	fi
325	# The EXIT trap dispatches release asynchronously w.r.t. this shell's `wait`
326	# on some platforms; give the marker a bounded moment to appear.
327	for _ in $(seq 1 50); do grep -q ':release' "$RELEASE_MARKER" 2>/dev/null && break; sleep 0.1; done
328	_assert_released "SPEC-4" intake build
329	
330	# ── SPEC-5: external hard kill (what an overrunning `timeout` produces) ──────
331	# ADR-053 §2: assert on an observable event, never a wall-clock budget.
332	#
333	# This case used to run the whole runner under `timeout 6`. Those 6 seconds had
334	# to cover process startup, template resolution AND reaching the build stage —
335	# so the budget was really a bet on host speed. Under the parallel pool (#991,
336	# the tier is parallel by default and the serial-pin list is empty) startup
337	# alone outran it: the runner was killed before any stage dispatched, the marker
338	# came back empty, and the failure read as a cleanup regression that standalone
339	# runs could never reproduce.
340	#
341	# The supervising timeout stays, but only as a runaway guard with a ceiling no
342	# healthy run approaches. The kill that this case actually asserts on is driven
343	# from BUILD_STARTED — the runner is provably inside the build stage — and
344	# escalates TERM→KILL the way `timeout` itself does, which is what separates
345	# this case from SPEC-4's plain SIGTERM.
346	print_test_section "SPEC-5: exit path = external hard kill (timeout-style)"
347	_prep timeout
348	export BUILD_RC=0 BUILD_SLEEP=1
349	_tbin=""
350	if   command -v gtimeout >/dev/null 2>&1; then _tbin=gtimeout
351	elif command -v timeout  >/dev/null 2>&1; then _tbin=timeout
352	fi
353	if [[ -z "$_tbin" ]]; then
354	    SKIP=$((SKIP + 1))
355	    echo -e "  ${YELLOW}SKIP${RESET}: [SPEC-5] external hard kill (no timeout binary available)" >&2
356	else
357	    # #2029: the force-kill grace must be DERIVED from the release budget, not a
358	    # hardcoded literal. _SPEC5_STAGE_TIMEOUT is the per-stage bound (after #1801
359	    # this is template_stage_time_limit — 30s in simple.yaml; 3s here is a
360	    # test-safe stand-in). Three stages release on this path, so the grace clears
361	    # 3x the per-hook bound. The hooks in this case return promptly; the grace is
362	    # only a runaway guard so a runner that ignores TERM cannot hang the suite.
363	    _SPEC5_STAGE_TIMEOUT=3
364	    _SPEC5_KILL_GRACE=$(( _SPEC5_STAGE_TIMEOUT * 3 + 6 ))   # 3 stages + margin
365	    set -m
366	    bash -c 'cd "$1" && exec "$4" 120 bash "$2" --template resume-minimal --goal "$3"' \
367	        _ "$OVERLAY_REPO" "$RUNNER" "release-timeout" "$_tbin" >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1 &
368	    RUNNER_PID=$!
369	    set +m
370	    for _ in $(seq 1 300); do [[ -s "$BUILD_STARTED" ]] && break; sleep 0.1; done
371	    kill -TERM -"$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || kill -TERM "$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
372	    ( sleep "$_SPEC5_KILL_GRACE"; kill -KILL -"$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || kill -KILL "$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true ) &
373	    _spec5_killer=$!
374	    wait "$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
375	    kill "$_spec5_killer" 2>/dev/null || true
376	    wait "$_spec5_killer" 2>/dev/null || true
377	    for _ in $(seq 1 50); do grep -q ':release' "$RELEASE_MARKER" 2>/dev/null && break; sleep 0.1; done
378	    _assert_released "SPEC-5" intake build
379	fi
380	
381	# ── SPEC-6: a blocking cleanup hook cannot hold the exit open ────────────────
382	# The dispatch runs inside the EXIT trap, so an unbounded hook would turn a
383	# normal exit into a hang — the same class of bug (a process that outlives the
384	# run) that this mechanism exists to prevent.
385	print_test_section "SPEC-6: a cleanup hook that blocks cannot hang the runner"
386	wait "$_SPEC6_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
387	CASE_DIR="$_SPEC6_DIR"
388	_elapsed="$(cat "$CASE_DIR/elapsed" 2>/dev/null || echo 999)"
389	# The blocking hook sleeps 120s. The bound is the release stage's own
390	# `timeout_s:` at the top-level stage block (read by template_stage_time_limit
391	# after #1801 — 30s in simple.yaml), so the runner returns in about 30s.
392	# Allow generous headroom for a loaded host while still failing an unbounded wait.
393	if [[ "$_elapsed" -lt 60 ]]; then
394	    assert_pass "[SPEC-6] blocking cleanup is bounded (runner exited in ${_elapsed}s)"
395	else
396	    assert_fail "[SPEC-6] blocking cleanup is bounded" "runner took ${_elapsed}s"
397	fi
398	# #2287: the bound must stop the hook, not just stop waiting for it. Before,
399	# the hook lived on after the run, finished its sleep ~2 min later, and wrote
400	# into a state folder the run no longer owned. The kills are sent before the
401	# runner returns; up to 1s covers the killed processes exiting on a loaded host.
402	_hook_pid="$(head -n 1 "$CASE_DIR/hook.pid" 2>/dev/null || true)"
403	if [[ -n "$_hook_pid" ]]; then
404	    for _ in $(seq 1 10); do kill -0 "$_hook_pid" 2>/dev/null || break; sleep 0.1; done
405	fi
406	if [[ -z "$_hook_pid" ]]; then
407	    assert_fail "[SPEC-6] fixture: the blocking hook recorded its pid" "no $CASE_DIR/hook.pid"
408	elif kill -0 "$_hook_pid" 2>/dev/null; then
409	    assert_fail "[SPEC-6] the blocked hook does not outlive the run" "pid $_hook_pid still alive after the runner returned"
410	    # Leave nothing behind for the rest of the suite: the hook first, so it
411	    # cannot carry on once its sleep ends, then the sleep it leaves orphaned.
412	    _hook_kids="$(pgrep -P "$_hook_pid" 2>/dev/null || true)"
413	    kill -KILL "$_hook_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
414	    for _k in $_hook_kids; do kill -KILL "$_k" 2>/dev/null || true; done
415	else
416	    assert_pass "[SPEC-6] the blocked hook does not outlive the run"
417	fi
418	
419	# ── SPEC-6b (#2333): a child that ignores TERM is killed too ────────────────
420	# The bound sends TERM to the hook's group, then KILL after a grace. The runner
421	# waited only for the group leader and cancelled the watchdog when it exited, so
422	# a member that ignored TERM never got the KILL and outlived the run.
423	print_test_section "SPEC-6b: a hook child that ignores TERM does not outlive the run"
424	# The time bound itself is SPEC-6's check, on the same dispatch path; this
425	# case is only about what survives it.
426	wait "$_SPEC6B_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
427	CASE_DIR="$_SPEC6B_DIR"
428	_child_pid=""
429	for _ in $(seq 1 50); do
430	    _child_pid="$(head -n 1 "$CASE_DIR/hook-child.pid" 2>/dev/null || true)"
431	    [[ -n "$_child_pid" ]] && break; sleep 0.1
432	done
433	_alive=1
434	# Only poll a pid that was recorded; a missing pid is reported as a fixture failure below.
435	if [[ -n "$_child_pid" ]]; then
436	    for _ in $(seq 1 50); do kill -0 "$_child_pid" 2>/dev/null || { _alive=0; break; }; sleep 0.1; done
437	fi
438	if [[ -z "$_child_pid" ]]; then
439	    assert_fail "[SPEC-6b] fixture: the child recorded its pid" "no $CASE_DIR/hook-child.pid"
440	elif [[ "$_alive" -eq 1 ]]; then
441	    assert_fail "[SPEC-6b] a hook child that ignores TERM does not outlive the run" "pid $_child_pid still alive 5s after the runner returned"
442	    kill -KILL "$_child_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
443	else
444	    assert_pass "[SPEC-6b] a hook child that ignores TERM does not outlive the run"
445	fi
446	
447	# ── [#1801/SPEC-5]: _runner_dispatch_always_run uses template_stage_time_limit ──
448	# A blocking hook under a template with `timeout_s: 5` for release (top-level)
449	# must stop in ~5s, NOT in ~30s (router.timeout_s: 30 inherited from simple).
450	# Old code reads _TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT_release (router.timeout_s = 30) and
451	# uses that as the watchdog → runner takes ~30s.
452	# New code reads template_stage_time_limit("release") = 5 → runner takes ~5s.
453	# Assertion at < 20s: FAILS on old code (~30s), PASSES on new code (~5s).
454	print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-5]: always-run watchdog bound by timeout_s: (not router.timeout_s)"
455	wait "$_SPEC5_BOUND_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
456	CASE_DIR="$_SPEC5_BOUND_DIR"
457	_spec5_elapsed="$(cat "$CASE_DIR/elapsed" 2>/dev/null || echo 999)"
458	if [[ "$_spec5_elapsed" -lt 20 ]]; then
459	    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-5] always-run watchdog uses timeout_s: 5 (runner exited in ${_spec5_elapsed}s; would be ~30s with router.timeout_s)"
460	else
461	    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-5] always-run watchdog uses timeout_s: 5" \
462	        "runner took ${_spec5_elapsed}s — expected < 20s (timeout_s: 5); old code would use router.timeout_s: 30"
463	fi
464	
465	# [#1801/SPEC-5] static guard: ZBUILD_RELEASE_TIMEOUT must not appear in runner.sh.
466	# Old code reads ZBUILD_RELEASE_TIMEOUT for the always-run watchdog; new code reads
467	# template_stage_time_limit instead. This grep fails on old code (the var is there)
468	# and passes on new code (it has been removed).
469	if ! grep -q 'ZBUILD_RELEASE_TIMEOUT' "$RUNNER"; then
470	    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-5] runner.sh does not reference ZBUILD_RELEASE_TIMEOUT (removed in #1801)"
471	else
472	    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-5] runner.sh must not reference ZBUILD_RELEASE_TIMEOUT" \
473	        "ZBUILD_RELEASE_TIMEOUT still present in $RUNNER; must be replaced by template_stage_time_limit"
474	fi
475	
476	# [#1801/SPEC-5] static guard: _runner_dispatch_always_run must not reference
477	# router.timeout_s (its bash manifestation: _TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT_*).
478	# Old code (runner.sh): local _ar_to_var="_TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT_${_ar_safe}"
479	# which reads router.timeout_s from the template config.
480	# New code: reads template_stage_time_limit instead.
481	# This grep fails on old code (the string is present) and passes on new (removed).
482	if ! grep -q '_TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT' "$RUNNER"; then
483	    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-5] runner.sh does not reference _TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT (router.timeout_s removed from always-run watchdog in #1801)"
484	else
485	    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-5] runner.sh must not reference _TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT (router.timeout_s)" \
486	        "_TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT still present in $RUNNER; must be replaced by template_stage_time_limit"
487	fi
488	
489	# [#1801/SPEC-5] static: shipped templates carry timeout_s: at stage level ──────
490	# template_stage_time_limits_load reads timeout_s: at stage-level indent (2
491	# spaces from the stage name at column 0, NOT inside `router:` at 4 spaces).
492	# These assertions verify that simple.yaml and deployed.yaml carry the correct
493	# values directly under the stage block — so the watchdog reads them, not
494	# router.timeout_s.
495	#
496	# Old code: these values might not exist or might only be under router:
497	#   → awk extracts nothing (or wrong value) → assertion fails on old code ✓
498	# New code: values are present at stage level → assertions pass ✓
499	print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-5] static: simple.yaml and deployed.yaml carry timeout_s: at stage level"
500	
501	_SIMPLE_YAML="$REPO_ROOT/config/templates/simple.yaml"
502	_DEPLOYED_YAML="$REPO_ROOT/config/templates/deployed.yaml"
503	
504	# Extract stage-level timeout_s: for release in simple.yaml.
505	# awk: enter release: section, stop at next top-level key (0-indent), stop
506	# inside router: sub-section, only match `  timeout_s:` (exactly 2 leading spaces).
507	_simple_release_ts="$(awk '
508	    /^release:/{in_r=1;in_sub=0;next}
509	    in_r && /^[a-zA-Z]/{in_r=0}
510	    in_r && /^  [a-zA-Z]/ && !/^  timeout_s:/{
511	        if ($0 ~ /^  router:/) { in_sub=1 } else { in_sub=0 }
512	        next
513	    }
514	    in_r && !in_sub && /^  timeout_s:/{
515	        sub(/^[[:space:]]*timeout_s:[[:space:]]*/, ""); print; exit
516	    }
517	' "$_SIMPLE_YAML" 2>/dev/null || printf '')"
518	
519	if [[ "$_simple_release_ts" == "30" ]]; then
520	    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-5] simple.yaml: release.timeout_s is 30 at stage level (not under router:)"
521	else
522	    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-5] simple.yaml: release.timeout_s must be 30 at stage level" \
523	        "got: '${_simple_release_ts:-<not found>}'; template_stage_time_limits_load reads 2-space indent, not router.timeout_s"
524	fi
525	
526	# Extract stage-level timeout_s: for persist in simple.yaml.
527	_simple_persist_ts="$(awk '
528	    /^persist:/{in_r=1;in_sub=0;next}
529	    in_r && /^[a-zA-Z]/{in_r=0}
530	    in_r && /^  [a-zA-Z]/ && !/^  timeout_s:/{
531	        if ($0 ~ /^  router:/) { in_sub=1 } else { in_sub=0 }
532	        next
533	    }
534	    in_r && !in_sub && /^  timeout_s:/{
535	        sub(/^[[:space:]]*timeout_s:[[:space:]]*/, ""); print; exit
536	    }
537	' "$_SIMPLE_YAML" 2>/dev/null || printf '')"
538	
539	if [[ "$_simple_persist_ts" == "120" ]]; then
540	    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-5] simple.yaml: persist.timeout_s is 120 at stage level"
541	else
542	    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-5] simple.yaml: persist.timeout_s must be 120 at stage level" \
543	        "got: '${_simple_persist_ts:-<not found>}'"
544	fi
545	
546	# deployed.yaml: same values.
547	_deployed_release_ts="$(awk '
548	    /^release:/{in_r=1;in_sub=0;next}
549	    in_r && /^[a-zA-Z]/{in_r=0}
550	    in_r && /^  [a-zA-Z]/ && !/^  timeout_s:/{
551	        if ($0 ~ /^  router:/) { in_sub=1 } else { in_sub=0 }
552	        next
553	    }
554	    in_r && !in_sub && /^  timeout_s:/{
555	        sub(/^[[:space:]]*timeout_s:[[:space:]]*/, ""); print; exit
556	    }
557	' "$_DEPLOYED_YAML" 2>/dev/null || printf '')"
558	
559	if [[ "$_deployed_release_ts" == "30" ]]; then
560	    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-5] deployed.yaml: release.timeout_s is 30 at stage level"
561	else
562	    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-5] deployed.yaml: release.timeout_s must be 30 at stage level" \
563	        "got: '${_deployed_release_ts:-<not found>}'"
564	fi
565	
566	_deployed_persist_ts="$(awk '
567	    /^persist:/{in_r=1;in_sub=0;next}
568	    in_r && /^[a-zA-Z]/{in_r=0}
569	    in_r && /^  [a-zA-Z]/ && !/^  timeout_s:/{
570	        if ($0 ~ /^  router:/) { in_sub=1 } else { in_sub=0 }
571	        next
572	    }
573	    in_r && !in_sub && /^  timeout_s:/{
574	        sub(/^[[:space:]]*timeout_s:[[:space:]]*/, ""); print; exit
575	    }
576	' "$_DEPLOYED_YAML" 2>/dev/null || printf '')"
577	
578	if [[ "$_deployed_persist_ts" == "120" ]]; then
579	    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-5] deployed.yaml: persist.timeout_s is 120 at stage level"
580	else
581	    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-5] deployed.yaml: persist.timeout_s must be 120 at stage level" \
582	        "got: '${_deployed_persist_ts:-<not found>}'"
583	fi
584	
585	cleanup_test_env
586	print_test_results
587	exit $((FAIL > 0))

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Integration test (#1829, ADR-054 §7): the runner dispatches cleanup(release)
# on EVERY exit path from a run — success, non-zero rc, the SIGINT propagation
# chain, an external SIGTERM, and an external timeout.
#
# This is the acceptance criterion the mechanism exists for: a stage's live
# resources must be freed however the run ends. A single missed exit path leaks
# whatever that stage spawned (#1748: suites observed alive 15+ min after exit).
#
# Why SIGINT is driven by the stage rather than `kill -INT`: this harness starts
# non-interactively with SIGINT inherited as SIG_IGN, and POSIX forbids a child
# from un-ignoring it — so `kill -INT` is silently dropped and the assertion
# would pass standalone while proving nothing. The repo's existing
# sigint-aborts-pipeline-test.sh drives the same chain the same way: the child
# returns 130, which is exactly what the kernel produces on Ctrl-C. Since #1850
# (ADR-054 §4, ADR-025) a signal is a recorded WORD, not an rc, so the stage
# also arms the abort sentinel (empty = sigint), as the runner's INT trap in
# the process group would.
#
# Assertion in every case: the stub stages' cleanup hooks recorded `release`
# (and never `purge`) in the marker file.
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
RUNNER="$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/runner.sh"

# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"

print_test_header "runner dispatches cleanup(release) on every exit path (#1829)"
setup_test_env "runner-release-exit-paths"
export ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=warn

PLUGINS_ROOT="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/plugins"
export ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT="$PLUGINS_ROOT"
export ZBUILD_EVENT_SCHEMA="$REPO_ROOT/config/event-schema.json"
export ZBUILD_MODELS_FILE="$REPO_ROOT/config/models.json"
export ZBUILD_CYCLES_ENABLED=0
mkdir -p "$PLUGINS_ROOT"

# The teardown plugin resolves its repo root by walking three levels up from
# its own directory (plugin-bootstrap), using a LOGICAL pwd — so symlinking the
# plugin itself would resolve to TEST_TEMP_DIR and fail to find helpers.sh.
# Give TEST_TEMP_DIR the shape of a repo root instead, then copy teardown in.
ln -s "$REPO_ROOT/scripts" "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/scripts"
ln -s "$REPO_ROOT/core"    "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/core"
mkdir -p "$PLUGINS_ROOT/tool"
cp -R "$REPO_ROOT/plugins/tool/teardown" "$PLUGINS_ROOT/tool/teardown"

mock_plugin_factory "intake" "agent" 0 >/dev/null
mock_plugin_factory "build"  "agent" 0 >/dev/null
mock_plugin_factory "test"   "tool"  0 >/dev/null

# Declare the optional cleanup hook — without it plugin_hook_call emits
# `plugin.cleanup.absent`, returns 0 (#1823: rc is binary), and the stage is a
# no-op rather than a witness.
# Re-emit the manifest rather than appending: `cleanup:` has to sit inside the
# contiguous `hooks:` block, and mock_plugin_factory already wrote `requires:`
# after it. #1850/#2366: the re-emitted manifest keeps the factory's declaration —
# result_contract 3 and a JSON primary each run hook below writes.
for _spec in "agent/intake:intake:intake_cleanup" "agent/build:build:build_cleanup" "tool/test:test:test_cleanup"; do
    _dir="${_spec%%:*}"; _rest="${_spec#*:}"; _id="${_rest%%:*}"; _fn="${_rest#*:}"
    _kind="${_dir%%/*}"
    cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/$_dir/manifest.yaml" <<EOF
id: $_id
name: Test $_id
kind: $_kind
version: 0.0.1
hooks:
  run: ${_id//-/_}_run
  cleanup: $_fn
requires:
  core:
    - redaction
provides:
  result_contract: 3
outputs:
  - id: ${_id//-/_}_result
    path: \${artifact_dir}/${_id}-result.json
    type: ${_id}-result.json@1
    format: json
    required: true
    primary: true
EOF
done

# Stubs: run honours env-driven rc/sleep; cleanup records "<stage>:<scope>".
cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/agent/intake/plugin.sh" <<'PLUG'
intake_run() {
    local _art; _art="${ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR:-$(dirname "$2")/artifacts}"; mkdir -p "$_art"
    printf '%s' '{"result_contract":3,"outcome":"pass","reason":"stub"}' > "$_art/intake-result.json"
    return 0
}
intake_cleanup() { printf 'intake:%s\n' "${3:-NOSCOPE}" >> "${RELEASE_MARKER}"; return 0; }
PLUG
cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/agent/build/plugin.sh" <<'PLUG'
build_run() {
    printf '%s\n' "$BASHPID" > "${BUILD_STARTED:-/dev/null}"
    if [[ "${BUILD_SLEEP:-0}" == "1" ]]; then
        local _i; for _i in $(seq 1 300); do sleep 0.1; done
    fi
    local _art; _art="${ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR:-$(dirname "$2")/artifacts}"; mkdir -p "$_art"
    [[ "${BUILD_ARM_ABORT:-0}" == "1" ]] && : > "${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR}/.abort.signal"
    if [[ "${BUILD_RC:-0}" == "0" ]]; then
        printf '%s' '{"result_contract":3,"outcome":"pass","reason":"stub"}' > "$_art/build-result.json"
    else
        printf '%s' '{"result_contract":3,"outcome":"broken","reason":"stub failure"}' > "$_art/build-result.json"
    fi
    return "${BUILD_RC:-0}"
}
build_cleanup() {
    printf 'build:%s\n' "${3:-NOSCOPE}" >> "${RELEASE_MARKER}"
    # A hook that never returns — used to prove the dispatch is bounded. It
    # records its own pid so SPEC-6 can check it does not outlive the run (#2287).
    if [[ "${BLOCK_CLEANUP:-0}" == "1" ]]; then
        printf '%s\n' "$BASHPID" >> "${RELEASE_MARKER%/*}/hook.pid"
        sleep 120
    fi
    if [[ "${BLOCK_CLEANUP_IGNORE_TERM:-0}" == "1" ]]; then
        # #2333: a child that ignores TERM, under a hook shell that does not.
        ( trap '' TERM; printf '%s\n' "$BASHPID" >> "${RELEASE_MARKER%/*}/hook-child.pid"; sleep 120 ) &
        wait
    fi
    return 0
}

OVERLAY_REPO="$(setup_git_temp_repo release-exit-paths-repo)"
install_template_overlay "$OVERLAY_REPO" resume-minimal
export ZBUILD_SCOPE_OVERRIDE=1
mkdir -p "$HOME/.zbuild"
printf '%s' "bootstrap" > "$HOME/.zbuild/scope-override-token"

_case_no=0
# _prep <name> — fresh state dir + marker for one exit path.
_prep() {
    _case_no=$((_case_no + 1))
    CASE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/case-$_case_no-$1"

# _assert_released <case> <stage>... — EVERY named stage released, purge never.
#
# #1989: this used to grep the shared marker for any ':release' and pass. Three
# stages append to that one file, so one stage releasing masked two that never
# did — measured: neutering build_cleanup alone left the suite green, and it
# took neutering all three to turn it red. The assertion could only ever detect
# a TOTAL failure of the mechanism, never a partial one, which is the shape a
# real regression takes (#1748: suites observed alive 15+ min after exit).
#
# Each case now names the stages whose cleanup must have run. The sets differ
# by exit path because a stage only reaches release once it has been dispatched.
#
# ADR-062 §2: reclamation reads the process group recorded at DISPATCH, not the
# completion status map, so a stage killed mid-flight IS reclaimable. SPEC-4 and
# SPEC-5 therefore expect `build` as well as `intake` — build had demonstrably
# started (it wrote BUILD_STARTED) before the signal landed. Before #2001 both
# freed `intake` only, because teardown iterated `.stage_statuses`, which
# `_update_stage_status` writes only on complete/failed — i.e. after a stage
# returns, which a killed stage never does.
_assert_released() {
    local _case="$1"; shift
    local _marker; _marker="$(cat "$RELEASE_MARKER" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    local _stage _missing=""
    for _stage in "$@"; do
        grep -q "^${_stage}:release$" <<< "$_marker" || _missing="${_missing}${_stage} "
    done
    if [[ -z "$_missing" ]]; then
        assert_pass "[$_case] cleanup dispatched with scope=release for: $*"
    else
        assert_fail "[$_case] cleanup dispatched with scope=release for: $*" \
            "no release from: ${_missing}| marker=$(tr '\n' ' ' <<< "$_marker")"
    fi
    if grep -q ':purge' <<< "$_marker"; then
        assert_fail "[$_case] purge is never reachable from a run" "marker contained purge"
    else
        assert_pass "[$_case] purge is never reachable from a run"
    fi
}

# SPEC-6 and SPEC-6b each wait out the release bound on purpose: their hook
# blocks, and the bound (the base template's release `timeout_s:` at the
# top-level stage block, 30s after #1801) is what ends it. Started here, each
# from its own repo, so that bound runs while SPEC-1..5 do; their assertions
# are made below, in order.
#
# SPEC-5 (#1801): a separate blocking run uses a template with timeout_s: 5
# for release (NOT router.timeout_s: 5) — old code reads router.timeout_s: 30
# and takes ~30s; new code reads template_stage_time_limit (timeout_s: 5) and
# exits in ~5s. Started here so it runs in parallel with SPEC-6/6b.
_start_blocking() {   # <case name> <hook switch> [template-id]
    local _repo; _repo="$(setup_git_temp_repo "release-exit-paths-$1")"
    install_template_overlay "$_repo" resume-minimal
    local _tpl="${3:-resume-minimal}"
    (
        _prep "$1"
        export BUILD_RC=0 "$2"=1
        _t0=$(date +%s)
        ( cd "$_repo" && bash "$RUNNER" --template "$_tpl" --goal "release-$1" ) \
            >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1 || true
        printf '%s\n' "$(( $(date +%s) - _t0 ))" > "$CASE_DIR/elapsed"
    ) &
}
_start_blocking blocking BLOCK_CLEANUP;                   _SPEC6_PID=$!
_start_blocking blocking-ignore-term BLOCK_CLEANUP_IGNORE_TERM; _SPEC6B_PID=$!
_SPEC6_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/case-1-blocking"
_SPEC6B_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/case-1-blocking-ignore-term"

# [#1801/SPEC-5]: blocking run with timeout_s: 5 for release (top-level, read
# by template_stage_time_limit), while router.timeout_s: 30 is inherited from
# simple — distinguishes new code (uses timeout_s: 5) from old (router.timeout_s: 30).
_spec5_bound_repo="$(setup_git_temp_repo "release-exit-paths-spec5-bound")"
install_template_overlay "$_spec5_bound_repo" resume-minimal
if [[ -d "$_spec5_bound_repo/.git/info" ]] && \
   ! grep -qxF '/.zbuild/' "$_spec5_bound_repo/.git/info/exclude" 2>/dev/null; then
    printf '/.zbuild/\n' >> "$_spec5_bound_repo/.git/info/exclude"
fi
cat > "$_spec5_bound_repo/.zbuild/templates/resume-spec5-bound.yaml" <<'YAML'
id: resume-spec5-bound
extends: resume-minimal
release:
  timeout_s: 5
YAML
_start_blocking spec5-bound BLOCK_CLEANUP resume-spec5-bound; _SPEC5_BOUND_PID=$!
_SPEC5_BOUND_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/case-1-spec5-bound"

# ── SPEC-1: success ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
print_test_section "SPEC-1: exit path = success (rc 0)"
_prep success
export BUILD_RC=0
set +e
( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && bash "$RUNNER" --template resume-minimal --goal "release-success" ) \
    >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1
_rc=$?
set -e
# SPEC-6/6b run alongside this case; if it fails, say what the runner said.
[[ $_rc -eq 0 ]] || tail -20 "$CASE_DIR/out" >&2
assert_eq "[SPEC-1] runner exits 0 on the success path" "0" "$_rc"
_assert_released "SPEC-1" intake build test

# ── SPEC-2: non-zero stage rc ────────────────────────────────────────────────
print_test_section "SPEC-2: exit path = non-zero stage rc"
_prep nonzero
export BUILD_RC=1
set +e
( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && bash "$RUNNER" --template resume-minimal --goal "release-nonzero" ) \
    >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1
_rc=$?
set -e
if [[ "$_rc" -ne 0 ]]; then
    assert_pass "[SPEC-2] runner exits non-zero when a stage fails"
else
    assert_fail "[SPEC-2] runner exits non-zero when a stage fails" "rc=0"
fi
_assert_released "SPEC-2" intake build

# ── SPEC-3: SIGINT propagation chain (child rc=130 + abort word) ─────────────
print_test_section "SPEC-3: exit path = SIGINT chain (stage rc 130, sentinel armed)"
_prep sigint
export BUILD_RC=130 BUILD_ARM_ABORT=1
set +e
( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && bash "$RUNNER" --template resume-minimal --goal "release-sigint" ) \
    >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1
_rc=$?
set -e
# #1850: the run really took the SIGINT path — exit 1 (not 130) and the abort
# named sigint — or this case would only repeat SPEC-2's non-zero rc.
assert_eq "[SPEC-3] runner exits 1 on the SIGINT chain (not 130)" "1" "$_rc"
assert_eq "[SPEC-3] pipeline.aborted carries reason=sigint" "sigint" \
    "$(jq -r 'select(.type=="pipeline.aborted") | .data.reason // empty' "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL" 2>/dev/null | sort -u | tr -d '\n')"
_assert_released "SPEC-3" intake build

# ── SPEC-4: external SIGTERM ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
print_test_section "SPEC-4: exit path = external SIGTERM"
_prep sigterm
export BUILD_RC=0 BUILD_SLEEP=1
if command -v setsid >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    setsid bash -c 'cd "$1" && exec bash "$2" --template resume-minimal --goal "$3"' \
        _ "$OVERLAY_REPO" "$RUNNER" "release-sigterm" >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1 &
    RUNNER_PID=$!
else
    set -m
    bash -c 'cd "$1" && exec bash "$2" --template resume-minimal --goal "$3"' \
        _ "$OVERLAY_REPO" "$RUNNER" "release-sigterm" >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1 &
    RUNNER_PID=$!
    set +m
fi
for _ in $(seq 1 300); do [[ -s "$BUILD_STARTED" ]] && break; sleep 0.1; done
_build_pid="$(head -n 1 "$BUILD_STARTED" 2>/dev/null || true)"
_t0=$(date +%s)
kill -TERM "$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
wait "$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
_elapsed=$(( $(date +%s) - _t0 ))
# ADR-054 §7: the runner acts on the signal while the stage is still running.
# Build holds for 30s; a runner that waits for it to return took 30s+ here.
if [[ "$_elapsed" -lt 15 ]]; then
    assert_pass "[SPEC-4] the runner stops without waiting for the stage (${_elapsed}s)"
else
    assert_fail "[SPEC-4] the runner stops without waiting for the stage" "took ${_elapsed}s; build holds 30s"
fi
if [[ -n "$_build_pid" ]] && kill -0 "$_build_pid" 2>/dev/null; then
    assert_fail "[SPEC-4] the stage does not outlive the run" "build pid $_build_pid still alive"
    kill -KILL "$_build_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
else
    assert_pass "[SPEC-4] the stage does not outlive the run"
fi
# The EXIT trap dispatches release asynchronously w.r.t. this shell's `wait`
# on some platforms; give the marker a bounded moment to appear.
for _ in $(seq 1 50); do grep -q ':release' "$RELEASE_MARKER" 2>/dev/null && break; sleep 0.1; done
_assert_released "SPEC-4" intake build

# ── SPEC-5: external hard kill (what an overrunning `timeout` produces) ──────
# ADR-053 §2: assert on an observable event, never a wall-clock budget.
#
# This case used to run the whole runner under `timeout 6`. Those 6 seconds had
# to cover process startup, template resolution AND reaching the build stage —
# so the budget was really a bet on host speed. Under the parallel pool (#991,
# the tier is parallel by default and the serial-pin list is empty) startup
# alone outran it: the runner was killed before any stage dispatched, the marker
# came back empty, and the failure read as a cleanup regression that standalone
# runs could never reproduce.
#
# The supervising timeout stays, but only as a runaway guard with a ceiling no
# healthy run approaches. The kill that this case actually asserts on is driven
# from BUILD_STARTED — the runner is provably inside the build stage — and
# escalates TERM→KILL the way `timeout` itself does, which is what separates
# this case from SPEC-4's plain SIGTERM.
print_test_section "SPEC-5: exit path = external hard kill (timeout-style)"
_prep timeout
export BUILD_RC=0 BUILD_SLEEP=1
_tbin=""
if   command -v gtimeout >/dev/null 2>&1; then _tbin=gtimeout
elif command -v timeout  >/dev/null 2>&1; then _tbin=timeout
fi
if [[ -z "$_tbin" ]]; then
    SKIP=$((SKIP + 1))
    echo -e "  ${YELLOW}SKIP${RESET}: [SPEC-5] external hard kill (no timeout binary available)" >&2
else
    # #2029: the force-kill grace must be DERIVED from the release budget, not a
    # hardcoded literal. _SPEC5_STAGE_TIMEOUT is the per-stage bound (after #1801
    # this is template_stage_time_limit — 30s in simple.yaml; 3s here is a
    # test-safe stand-in). Three stages release on this path, so the grace clears
    # 3x the per-hook bound. The hooks in this case return promptly; the grace is
    # only a runaway guard so a runner that ignores TERM cannot hang the suite.
    _SPEC5_STAGE_TIMEOUT=3
    _SPEC5_KILL_GRACE=$(( _SPEC5_STAGE_TIMEOUT * 3 + 6 ))   # 3 stages + margin
    set -m
    bash -c 'cd "$1" && exec "$4" 120 bash "$2" --template resume-minimal --goal "$3"' \
        _ "$OVERLAY_REPO" "$RUNNER" "release-timeout" "$_tbin" >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1 &
    RUNNER_PID=$!
    set +m
    for _ in $(seq 1 300); do [[ -s "$BUILD_STARTED" ]] && break; sleep 0.1; done
    kill -TERM -"$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || kill -TERM "$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
    ( sleep "$_SPEC5_KILL_GRACE"; kill -KILL -"$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || kill -KILL "$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true ) &
    _spec5_killer=$!
    wait "$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
    kill "$_spec5_killer" 2>/dev/null || true
    wait "$_spec5_killer" 2>/dev/null || true
    for _ in $(seq 1 50); do grep -q ':release' "$RELEASE_MARKER" 2>/dev/null && break; sleep 0.1; done
    _assert_released "SPEC-5" intake build
fi

# ── SPEC-6: a blocking cleanup hook cannot hold the exit open ────────────────
# The dispatch runs inside the EXIT trap, so an unbounded hook would turn a
# normal exit into a hang — the same class of bug (a process that outlives the
# run) that this mechanism exists to prevent.
print_test_section "SPEC-6: a cleanup hook that blocks cannot hang the runner"
wait "$_SPEC6_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
CASE_DIR="$_SPEC6_DIR"
_elapsed="$(cat "$CASE_DIR/elapsed" 2>/dev/null || echo 999)"
# The blocking hook sleeps 120s. The bound is the release stage's own
# `timeout_s:` at the top-level stage block (read by template_stage_time_limit
# after #1801 — 30s in simple.yaml), so the runner returns in about 30s.
# Allow generous headroom for a loaded host while still failing an unbounded wait.
if [[ "$_elapsed" -lt 60 ]]; then
    assert_pass "[SPEC-6] blocking cleanup is bounded (runner exited in ${_elapsed}s)"
else
    assert_fail "[SPEC-6] blocking cleanup is bounded" "runner took ${_elapsed}s"
fi
# #2287: the bound must stop the hook, not just stop waiting for it. Before,
# the hook lived on after the run, finished its sleep ~2 min later, and wrote
# into a state folder the run no longer owned. The kills are sent before the
# runner returns; up to 1s covers the killed processes exiting on a loaded host.
_hook_pid="$(head -n 1 "$CASE_DIR/hook.pid" 2>/dev/null || true)"
if [[ -n "$_hook_pid" ]]; then
    for _ in $(seq 1 10); do kill -0 "$_hook_pid" 2>/dev/null || break; sleep 0.1; done
fi
if [[ -z "$_hook_pid" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[SPEC-6] fixture: the blocking hook recorded its pid" "no $CASE_DIR/hook.pid"
elif kill -0 "$_hook_pid" 2>/dev/null; then
    assert_fail "[SPEC-6] the blocked hook does not outlive the run" "pid $_hook_pid still alive after the runner returned"
    # Leave nothing behind for the rest of the suite: the hook first, so it
    # cannot carry on once its sleep ends, then the sleep it leaves orphaned.
    _hook_kids="$(pgrep -P "$_hook_pid" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    kill -KILL "$_hook_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
    for _k in $_hook_kids; do kill -KILL "$_k" 2>/dev/null || true; done
else
    assert_pass "[SPEC-6] the blocked hook does not outlive the run"
fi

# ── SPEC-6b (#2333): a child that ignores TERM is killed too ────────────────
# The bound sends TERM to the hook's group, then KILL after a grace. The runner
# waited only for the group leader and cancelled the watchdog when it exited, so
# a member that ignored TERM never got the KILL and outlived the run.
print_test_section "SPEC-6b: a hook child that ignores TERM does not outlive the run"
# The time bound itself is SPEC-6's check, on the same dispatch path; this
# case is only about what survives it.
wait "$_SPEC6B_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
CASE_DIR="$_SPEC6B_DIR"
_child_pid=""
for _ in $(seq 1 50); do
    _child_pid="$(head -n 1 "$CASE_DIR/hook-child.pid" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    [[ -n "$_child_pid" ]] && break; sleep 0.1
done
_alive=1
# Only poll a pid that was recorded; a missing pid is reported as a fixture failure below.
if [[ -n "$_child_pid" ]]; then
    for _ in $(seq 1 50); do kill -0 "$_child_pid" 2>/dev/null || { _alive=0; break; }; sleep 0.1; done
fi
if [[ -z "$_child_pid" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[SPEC-6b] fixture: the child recorded its pid" "no $CASE_DIR/hook-child.pid"
elif [[ "$_alive" -eq 1 ]]; then
    assert_fail "[SPEC-6b] a hook child that ignores TERM does not outlive the run" "pid $_child_pid still alive 5s after the runner returned"
    kill -KILL "$_child_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
else
    assert_pass "[SPEC-6b] a hook child that ignores TERM does not outlive the run"
fi

# ── [#1801/SPEC-5]: _runner_dispatch_always_run uses template_stage_time_limit ──
# A blocking hook under a template with `timeout_s: 5` for release (top-level)
# must stop in ~5s, NOT in ~30s (router.timeout_s: 30 inherited from simple).
# Old code reads _TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT_release (router.timeout_s = 30) and
# uses that as the watchdog → runner takes ~30s.
# New code reads template_stage_time_limit("release") = 5 → runner takes ~5s.
# Assertion at < 20s: FAILS on old code (~30s), PASSES on new code (~5s).
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-5]: always-run watchdog bound by timeout_s: (not router.timeout_s)"
wait "$_SPEC5_BOUND_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
CASE_DIR="$_SPEC5_BOUND_DIR"
_spec5_elapsed="$(cat "$CASE_DIR/elapsed" 2>/dev/null || echo 999)"
if [[ "$_spec5_elapsed" -lt 20 ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-5] always-run watchdog uses timeout_s: 5 (runner exited in ${_spec5_elapsed}s; would be ~30s with router.timeout_s)"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-5] always-run watchdog uses timeout_s: 5" \
        "runner took ${_spec5_elapsed}s — expected < 20s (timeout_s: 5); old code would use router.timeout_s: 30"
fi

# [#1801/SPEC-5] static guard: ZBUILD_RELEASE_TIMEOUT must not appear in runner.sh.
# Old code reads ZBUILD_RELEASE_TIMEOUT for the always-run watchdog; new code reads
# template_stage_time_limit instead. This grep fails on old code (the var is there)
# and passes on new code (it has been removed).
if ! grep -q 'ZBUILD_RELEASE_TIMEOUT' "$RUNNER"; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-5] runner.sh does not reference ZBUILD_RELEASE_TIMEOUT (removed in #1801)"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-5] runner.sh must not reference ZBUILD_RELEASE_TIMEOUT" \
        "ZBUILD_RELEASE_TIMEOUT still present in $RUNNER; must be replaced by template_stage_time_limit"
fi

# [#1801/SPEC-5] static guard: _runner_dispatch_always_run must not reference
# router.timeout_s (its bash manifestation: _TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT_*).
# Old code (runner.sh): local _ar_to_var="_TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT_${_ar_safe}"
# which reads router.timeout_s from the template config.
# New code: reads template_stage_time_limit instead.
# This grep fails on old code (the string is present) and passes on new (removed).
if ! grep -q '_TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT' "$RUNNER"; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-5] runner.sh does not reference _TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT (router.timeout_s removed from always-run watchdog in #1801)"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-5] runner.sh must not reference _TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT (router.timeout_s)" \
        "_TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT still present in $RUNNER; must be replaced by template_stage_time_limit"
fi

# [#1801/SPEC-5] static: shipped templates carry timeout_s: at stage level ──────
# template_stage_time_limits_load reads timeout_s: at stage-level indent (2
# spaces from the stage name at column 0, NOT inside `router:` at 4 spaces).
# These assertions verify that simple.yaml and deployed.yaml carry the correct
# values directly under the stage block — so the watchdog reads them, not
# router.timeout_s.
#
# Old code: these values might not exist or might only be under router:
#   → awk extracts nothing (or wrong value) → assertion fails on old code ✓
# New code: values are present at stage level → assertions pass ✓
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-5] static: simple.yaml and deployed.yaml carry timeout_s: at stage level"

_SIMPLE_YAML="$REPO_ROOT/config/templates/simple.yaml"
_DEPLOYED_YAML="$REPO_ROOT/config/templates/deployed.yaml"

# Extract stage-level timeout_s: for release in simple.yaml.
# awk: enter release: section, stop at next top-level key (0-indent), stop
# inside router: sub-section, only match `  timeout_s:` (exactly 2 leading spaces).
_simple_release_ts="$(awk '
    /^release:/{in_r=1;in_sub=0;next}
    in_r && /^[a-zA-Z]/{in_r=0}
    in_r && /^  [a-zA-Z]/ && !/^  timeout_s:/{
        if ($0 ~ /^  router:/) { in_sub=1 } else { in_sub=0 }
        next
    }
    in_r && !in_sub && /^  timeout_s:/{
        sub(/^[[:space:]]*timeout_s:[[:space:]]*/, ""); print; exit
    }
' "$_SIMPLE_YAML" 2>/dev/null || printf '')"

if [[ "$_simple_release_ts" == "30" ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-5] simple.yaml: release.timeout_s is 30 at stage level (not under router:)"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-5] simple.yaml: release.timeout_s must be 30 at stage level" \
        "got: '${_simple_release_ts:-<not found>}'; template_stage_time_limits_load reads 2-space indent, not router.timeout_s"
fi

# Extract stage-level timeout_s: for persist in simple.yaml.
_simple_persist_ts="$(awk '
    /^persist:/{in_r=1;in_sub=0;next}
    in_r && /^[a-zA-Z]/{in_r=0}
    in_r && /^  [a-zA-Z]/ && !/^  timeout_s:/{
        if ($0 ~ /^  router:/) { in_sub=1 } else { in_sub=0 }
        next
    }
    in_r && !in_sub && /^  timeout_s:/{
        sub(/^[[:space:]]*timeout_s:[[:space:]]*/, ""); print; exit
    }
' "$_SIMPLE_YAML" 2>/dev/null || printf '')"

if [[ "$_simple_persist_ts" == "120" ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-5] simple.yaml: persist.timeout_s is 120 at stage level"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-5] simple.yaml: persist.timeout_s must be 120 at stage level" \
        "got: '${_simple_persist_ts:-<not found>}'"
fi

# deployed.yaml: same values.
_deployed_release_ts="$(awk '
    /^release:/{in_r=1;in_sub=0;next}
    in_r && /^[a-zA-Z]/{in_r=0}
    in_r && /^  [a-zA-Z]/ && !/^  timeout_s:/{
        if ($0 ~ /^  router:/) { in_sub=1 } else { in_sub=0 }
        next
    }
    in_r && !in_sub && /^  timeout_s:/{
        sub(/^[[:space:]]*timeout_s:[[:space:]]*/, ""); print; exit
    }
' "$_DEPLOYED_YAML" 2>/dev/null || printf '')"

if [[ "$_deployed_release_ts" == "30" ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-5] deployed.yaml: release.timeout_s is 30 at stage level"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-5] deployed.yaml: release.timeout_s must be 30 at stage level" \
        "got: '${_deployed_release_ts:-<not found>}'"
fi

_deployed_persist_ts="$(awk '
    /^persist:/{in_r=1;in_sub=0;next}
    in_r && /^[a-zA-Z]/{in_r=0}
    in_r && /^  [a-zA-Z]/ && !/^  timeout_s:/{
        if ($0 ~ /^  router:/) { in_sub=1 } else { in_sub=0 }
        next
    }
    in_r && !in_sub && /^  timeout_s:/{
        sub(/^[[:space:]]*timeout_s:[[:space:]]*/, ""); print; exit
    }
' "$_DEPLOYED_YAML" 2>/dev/null || printf '')"

if [[ "$_deployed_persist_ts" == "120" ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-5] deployed.yaml: persist.timeout_s is 120 at stage level"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-5] deployed.yaml: persist.timeout_s must be 120 at stage level" \
        "got: '${_deployed_persist_ts:-<not found>}'"
fi

cleanup_test_env
print_test_results
exit $((FAIL > 0))

id: always-run-minimal
name: Always-Run Minimal Pipeline
extends: simple
defaults:
  strategy: fanout

# #1831 fixture: the smallest template that exercises `always_run:`.
#
# NEW shape (`flow:` + top-level sections) on purpose — but NOT because
# `always_run:` needs it. The key is shape-INDEPENDENT: `_tpl_parse_always_run`
# reads it straight from the file, and SPEC-6 in tests/unit/template-always-run-test.sh
# proves an old-shape template inherits it too. The new shape is used here only
# because it is the smaller fixture, and because it exercises the per-repo
# overlay's new-shape path alongside it.
#
# `outcome` is the only flow stage. Its plugin is replaced per-case by the test
# so one fixture can drive every exit path: rc=0, rc=1, SIGINT (rc=130), SIGTERM
# and a hang past the timeout. `release` is never in the flow — the whole point
# is that it runs anyway.
flow:
  - outcome

always_run:
  - release

outcome:
  gate: auto
  io:
    destinations: [file]
    tail_lines: 50

# timeout_s is deliberately small so the watchdog case does not stretch the
# suite's wall clock. The bound itself is what SPEC-5 asserts.
release:
  gate: auto
  roles: [teardown]
  timeout_s: 2
  router:
    timeout_s: 2
  io:
    destinations: [file]
    tail_lines: 50
